summary: Anna Filigenzi works in archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She became a member of the Italian Institute for Africa and the East in 1984, directed the Italian Archaeological Mission in Afghanistan in 2003, and held posts at Naples.

Anna Halafoff is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. She earned her BA at the University of Melbourne, an MLitt at the University of New England, and a PhD at Monash University before holding a post at Deakin University.

Anna Kamensky (1867–1952) was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at the Bestuzhev Courses and the University of Geneva (PhD 1921–1926), she served as Privatdozent in comparative religion at Geneva from circa 1928 to 1950.

Anna Kramskova specializes in Tibetology and linguistics. She earned her master's degree from Saint Petersburg State University in 2016 and served as a research assistant at the Institute of Linguistic Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences in 2019.
Anna M. Shields is a sinologist who taught at the University of Maryland, College Park from circa 2007 to 2015 before becoming Professor at Princeton University in 2015.

Anna Sawerthal is a Tibetologist who earned an MA at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, with instruction from Johanna Buß, and completed a PhD at Heidelberg University, having also studied under Dawa Tsering and Norbu Tashi.
Anna Scarabel is an Indologist who earned her PhD at Heidelberg University in 2018. Her faculty post at the University of Vienna is attested for 2026.

Anna Seidel (1938–1991) was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Max Kaltenmark and Rolf Alfred Stein. A member of EFEO, she worked at Institut du Hōbōgirin and founded Cahiers d'Extrême-Asie.

Anna Stirr is an Indologist who earned a BA at Lawrence University and a PhD at Columbia University. She held posts at The New School, Oxford, and Leiden before joining the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa in 2012.

Anna Szabolcsi is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences. She worked as a research fellow at HAS, became a professor at UCLA, and was appointed professor of linguistics at NYU circa 1998.
Anna Šebestová was an Indologist and linguist who completed her PhD at Charles University under the supervision of Josef Zubatý in 1919.

Anna-Pya Sjödin specializes in Indology and philosophy. She earned her PhD at Uppsala University in 2007, supervised by Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada, and also studied under Barbro Eriksson.
Annarao Kulkarni works in computational linguistics and Indology, holding posts at the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing and the Indian Heritage Language Computing Group.

Anncharlott Eschmann (1941–1977) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She studied at Munich and Marburg before completing her PhD at Heidelberg University, where she later served as an assistant in 1975.
Anne Burchardi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Erik Haarh and held a post at the National Museum of Denmark.

Anne Carolyn Klein is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religion who studied at Binghamton, Wisconsin-Madison, and Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. She became Professor and Chair of Religious Studies at Rice University and founded the Dawn Mountain Center.

Anne E. Monius (1964–2019) was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her undergraduate and graduate degrees at Harvard University and taught at the University of Virginia before becoming Professor of South Asian Religions at Harvard.

Anne Feldhaus is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. She studied at Manhattanville University and the University of Pennsylvania before joining Arizona State University in 1981, where she became Distinguished Foundation Professor and Emeritus Professor of Religious Studies.
Anne Hardgrove is a historian and Indologist who studied at Carleton College and the University of Michigan before taking up a post in history at the University of Texas at San Antonio in 2000.

Anne Hopkins Aitken (1911–1994) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Scripps College, Stanford, Northwestern, and Oxford. She co-founded the Honolulu Diamond Sangha in 1959 and also founded the Maui Zendo.
